benchmarks.note: Jeep Wrangler only, and the article credits RepairPal for the figure, so it is not a fully independent third estimate: parts about $1,100, labor about $600. No date shown on the page

finding: The live range of $280-$1,925 is too low at the bottom and about right at the top for the clutch kit alone, but it leaves no room for a flywheel. Built totals (clutch kit + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2020 Honda Civic 1.5L turbo about $1,268-$1,894 (5.3 hr); midsize 2018 Subaru WRX about $1,102-$1,441 (4.3-4.9 hr); truck 2019 Jeep Wrangler JL about $835-$1,391 (4.2-6 hr); luxury 2015 BMW 328i about $1,210-$1,872 (6 hr). Across the four that is roughly $835-$1,895. Nothing found supports $280: the cheapest kit priced here is $331 before any labor, the shortest stated time is 4.2 hours (about $504 of labor at $120/hr), and the lowest benchmark figure is $500 (ConsumerAffairs), with RepairPal's national average at $1,630-$2,047. A floor of roughly $800-$850 is the lowest we can build, and even that uses a genuine kit at a discounted online price plus a recall labor time, both less than a shop normally charges. Older, simpler cars with cheaper kits could come in under it, which is how ConsumerAffairs reaches $600 for economy cars, but no source loaded here stated the parts and hours to build such a figure. The $1,925 top matches the highest built total ($1,894), yet RepairPal's averages run to $2,047 nationally and $2,240-$2,632 on some models, and a flywheel (often replaced with the clutch, and expensive when it is a dual-mass type) is extra, so real quotes above $1,925 are common. How solid the labor times are: three of the four are manufacturer-stated times for the example vehicle itself. The Civic's 5.3 hr is a Honda warranty time that also covers replacing the flywheel and a wheel alignment, and is the only stated figure found for that car, so the economy range has no spread. The WRX's 4.3 hr is Subaru's warranty time for clutch replacement and its 4.9 hr is a Subaru time for a slightly larger clutch-system repair. The Wrangler's 4.2 hr is an FCA recall time for replacing the clutch assembly, and its 6 hr top is a parts retailer's '4-6 hours' estimate. The BMW figure is the weakest: no time for the F30 328i was found, and the 6 hr used is a parts seller's round figure for an older 3 Series (E46) job that includes the flywheel. Warranty and recall times are the low end of what shops bill. On parts: the Civic low is a mild performance kit because no plain replacement kit with confirmed fitment was found, and the Wrangler low is the genuine kit at a retailer's discount because the only aftermarket kits found are heavy-duty upgrades costing $1,165-$1,650. The WRX genuine figure is disc and cover only (the genuine release bearing price could not be loaded), and the catalog lists two discs and two covers for the same trims, so its high end could be $524-$657. Our totals sit below RepairPal's, mostly because RepairPal's parts figure ($809-$843) is higher than the kits priced here for three of the four vehicles. An estimate is never a quote and never a diagnosis.
extras: A quote often adds flywheel resurfacing or a new flywheel (a dual-mass flywheel can cost as much as the clutch kit or more; the one clutch-and-flywheel kit priced here was $1,165 against $331-$431 for the clutch parts alone), a pilot bearing or bushing, a rear main seal while the transmission is out, a clutch master or slave cylinder (on some vehicles the slave cylinder is inside the bell housing and is changed with the clutch), clutch hydraulic fluid and bleeding (Subaru lists 0.3 hr), transmission gear oil, new flywheel and pressure plate bolts, a wheel alignment where the subframe is lowered, a diagnosis or road-test fee, shop supplies and sales tax. All-wheel-drive and four-wheel-drive vehicles can take longer because a transfer case or extra driveshaft has to come off. Dual-clutch automatics are a different and dearer job and are not covered here.
